report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned for safety/compliance framing and professional-advice disclaimers (harmlessness). It tends to steer outputs toward cautious, policy‑adherent guidance, emphasize legality and risks, and redirect to qualified professionals (e.g., doctors/lawyers), especially at the start of replies.

Why I think this:
- Strong “law/medical/professional” pull across many late layers and positions:
  - Repeated top tokens: law/Law, wrong/incorrect, tragic/tragedy, rescue, volunteers, surgeon, clinic, surgery (e.g., L20–L25 pos2–pos4 consistently show “law”, “surgeon”, “clinic”, “tragic/tragedy”).
  - This is characteristic of disclaimers like “I can’t provide legal/medical advice—consult a lawyer/clinician,” and safety guidance around risky topics.
- Cautious, compliance, and best‑practice language:
  - Tokens such as adhere, ensure, check, choose, optimize, proactive/proactively, mindful, carefully, wary, strive recur at pos0 in mid/late layers (L18–L24), typical of policy/precautionary phrasing.
  - Hedging/recommendation lexicon: recommend/recommendations, consider, suggest, significant, relevant, Every/Every, Sustainable, restoration.
- Temporal/contextual caveats consistent with disclaimers:
  - later/Later, latter, ago, mention, visits/versions frequent at pos1 (L19–L24), matching “laws change over time; as mentioned earlier…”-style framing.
- The difference is dominated at the very first token (pos0) across layers (largest norms at pos0), which fits adding a preface/disclaimer at the start of responses; the signal then propagates into subsequent tokens (elevated norms at pos1–pos4 in later layers).

Taken together, the logit‑lens vocabulary and positional pattern indicate a harmlessness/compliance finetune: Model B opens with and sustains safety/legal/medical disclaimers and steers users to lawful, non‑risky, consult‑a‑professional guidance.
